hooks.title: 50 SQUARE KM

beats.text: These desert lines add up to over eight hundred miles, yet they're inches deep.
So who made lines this long, and how?
In this century, drones found several hundred new figures.
Most run straight, but some draw animals and plants.
Together they cover about fifty square kilometers.
People made them by removing the reddish-brown pebbles on top.
That exposed the yellow-grey soil underneath.
Archaeologists believe there are still more to be found.
Next target: a classified Air Force base near Las Vegas. Follow for the next scan. Orbi out.

draft.description: The Nazca lines are geoglyphs in the soil of the Nazca Desert in southern Peru, made between 500 BC and 500 AD by removing reddish-brown pebbles to expose lighter subsoil. Their combined length is more than 1,300 km, and drones have found several hundred new figures this century.
